chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Aban, from Abbad al-Dbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding the 'injin' (impotent man), when it is known that he is 'injin' and does not have intercourse with women, separation is effected between the two; and when he has intercourse with her with one thrust, they are not separated; and the man is not rejected due to a defect.

key_terms.عِنِّين: Impotent man (specifically one who cannot consummate marriage)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for a man who is impotent (injin) regarding marital separation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the legal threshold for 'khulu'' or separation due to impotence ('injin'), distinguishing between known, non-consummating cases and those where at least one valid intercourse has occurred. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that a physical defect does not automatically invalidate the marriage contract once consummation is proven, emphasizing the stability of the marital bond over specific physical capabilities.
